# PR 12950 follow-up retrospective

## Worked

Neutral public-history packet and pinned original/current source let both fresh reviewers reassess rather than defend the old review. The parser's explicit append branch answered the author's separator point directly. One targeted isolated parser run with previous-file control was sufficient; Sol source analysis added independent reasoning without manufacturing extra tests. Both full reports were saved before coordinator synthesis. No findings beyond resolution were invented.

## Deviations and remediation

Opus's first directory listing exceeded 60 lines (about 85), and a paired policy read exceeded the aggregate limit (80). Later policy reads were completed, all history preserved and no oversized persisted tool-result file was reported. The dispatch already stated the aggregate bound; assignment-local remediation now explicitly includes first listings and parallel outputs. This remains noncompliant process history.

Fixture audit found `! grep` did not distinguish expected no-match from read/tool error. Broad guard and ALL-PASS claims are excluded. Extracted wordinlist was exercised on constructed expected input, not parser output; runtime membership claims are withdrawn. Separate audit-addendum.md preserves the original report. Public evidence is limited to individually inspected c2/c4/c7 parser streams/status and t1/t2 shell-test outputs plus pinned source. Actual case provenance and positive expected outputs, corroborated by independent source reasoning, support the public claims despite the deficient negative check. The responsible assignment instructions now require exact negative predicate statuses and explicit producer-input provenance. No further experimental rerun was necessary to settle a material public question.

Coordinator fetch of an initially guessed TLP source filename failed with 404; retained transport receipts precede the successful pinned fetch. Initial Herdr `help` discovery failed, followed by supported --help/--skill complete reads before any lifecycle action. Neither failed discovery/fetch provided technical evidence.

## Limits and cleanup

Opus auto-loaded process-only memory index; no prior-PR technical conclusions reported. No memory deletion or edits. Session/model metadata independently verified without reading peer conclusions. Native CLI history retained outside assignment-owned evidence, as automatically managed history. No desktop or audio resources requested; no hardware/service/upgrade changes. One sandbox completed and exited, no background jobs remain per reviewer receipt. No pattern killing or source deletion. Reviewer panes preserved idle.

No Omadev issue identified. Improvement: enforce output budgets mechanically in future launch tooling, and make negative-status handling explicit in fixture helper templates. These are process improvements, not confirmed toolkit defects.

The drop-in now uses `USB_DENYLIST+=`. With TLP 1.10.2's real parser and synthetic configuration:

```text
Earlier drop-in: USB_DENYLIST="1234:5678"

712c0b3 (=)   seven Intel IDs only; earlier entry lost
c525346 (+=)  1234:5678 + seven Intel IDs
```

An explicit assignment in `/etc/tlp.conf` still replaces the combined list. The parser supplies the separating space, confirming that no leading space is needed inside the appended value. The updated shell test passes on the current files and rejects the previous `=` form.

**Verified:** The description now correctly names `USB_EXCLUDE_BTUSB` and distinguishes its class-based exemption from the explicit Intel-ID list. No additional issue was found in this follow-up's scope.
